title: POC SDK & Toolchain Interop Snapshot - 7/14/26
summary: Weekly POC checkpoint: reviewed SDK integration artifacts, surfaced a serialization mismatch in structured outputs, discussed function/tool calling fallbacks and KV cache invalidation strategy, and agreed on benchmark next steps and security docs to send.
next_steps: Redwood to send minimal repro for serialization mismatch (Priya) by 2026-07-16
Sanctuary to run 1-hour load test against staging with streaming enabled and share traces by 2026-07-20
Jordan to attach pricing delta for dedicated pilot if throughput increases >2x by 2026-07-18
Schedule security deep dive (KMS/HSM + audit logs) w/ Sanctuary security team for week of 2026-07-27
action_items: Priya Menon - Create small repo that reproduces protobuf/JSON schema mismatch and link to ticket - due 2026-07-16

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-14 14:00 PT | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Marcus; Rana, Evan, Sofia, Tom

[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Um this is the weekly snapshot for the POC — quick agenda, serialization check, SDK behavior, function/tool calling fallbacks, and security ask.
[00:12] Rana: thanks, Jordan. we only have 50 minutes so, uh, we'll try to be concise. big thing for us this week is the structured output mismatch we saw in staging.
[00:20] Priya: yeah right, and quick heads up we reproduced a variant of it — it's intermittent when streaming responses are chunked and the client expects a full JSON blob.
[00:30] Evan: to add, our mobile proxy is sometimes doing protobuf-to-json conversion and that combined with partial streams causes the SDK to error out with a parse exception — like a trailing comma or half-object.
[00:44] Sofia: it's low frequency but high impact because it kills the orchestration step downstream. we built a retry but it's noisy.
[00:52] Priya: okay so first theory: streaming + mobile proxy + client-side serializer. second theory: Redwood's function-calling framing sometimes emits tool-result fragments before the closing token. we saw similar with earlier model versions but shouldn't happen with the streaming contract.
[01:08] Marcus: note we have a fallback mode where we emit a single-field "partial_output": true and then a reserve token to mark completion, but that relies on the SDK honoring that contract. maybe the mobile SDK drops that metadata.
[01:24] Tom: quick q: is this a model-level behavior or an SDK framing problem? like, are tokens truncated mid-JSON because of batching?
[01:32] Priya: it's more framing. the runtime may flush a batch boundary after a KV cache miss and that produces a send chunk that the mobile converter treats as final.
[01:44] Jordan: ok, action: Priya will produce a minimal repro repo that uses the mobile proxy and streams a function call result mid-object so we can see exact bytes. also Jordan will loop in mobile SDK folks.

[02:02] Evan: aside from serialization, we want to confirm function/tool calling semantics when the tool is remote. Our orchestration sometimes routes tool calls to a private lambda in our VPC and hits a cold start; in that case the Redwood SDK should surface a clear retryable error, not a generic 500.
[02:18] Priya: agreed — we have a retry policy on the SDK level and also a server-side retry/backoff. there's also an option to mark tools as "local" or "remote" in the call schema which toggles optimistic timeouts. Did you enable that?
[02:32] Evan: we did not; good to know. where's that documented?
[02:36] Jordan: I'll share the tools doc and a short snippet in the Slack thread after. link: https://redwood.internal/docs/poc/tools-fallbacks (note: placeholder link).

[03:00] Rana: security — we have a compliance check coming up and they want to see KMS integration and audit logs for all tool invocations. can you confirm Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and HSM-backed keys?
[03:12] Marcus: yes, Redwood Private supports KMS integration; we can show a config sample for bringing your own key (BYOK) and HSM-backed signing. audit logs can be exported to your SIEM with per-request metadata.
[03:24] Sofia: what's the retention on the hosted plan again? our policy is 13 months.
[03:28] Marcus: hosted default is 90 days, but for Dedicated/Private you can configure retention up to 24 months. we'll include options in the security doc.

[03:40] Tom: latency question — in our load test we saw p50 210ms p95 980ms. We're using the hosted endpoint with 16k context. any quick levers?
[03:50] Priya: batching window and KV cache hits are the two big ones. also quantized model variants sometimes shave 20-30% off token time but there's a quality tradeoff. are you using prefix caching?
[04:03] Evan: yes, prefix caching but we flush it on user context switches which maybe invalidates aggressively.
[04:08] Priya: you can tune TTLs and use partial-key invalidation rather than full flush. Marcus will share exact runtime flags.

[04:20] Rana: cost concerns — we may need Dedicated if throughput doubles, but we need a clear estimate. Jordan you mentioned a "pricing delta"?
[04:28] Jordan: yeah I'll send a short spreadsheet comparing hosted per-token vs dedicated committed throughput. will include break-even points for 2x, 3x throughput.

[04:38] Evan: on SDK ergonomics, we found two pain points: 1) function signatures can't express optional complex args cleanly in mobile bindings, 2) error codes from tool calls are sparse.
[04:50] Priya: for (1) we can add a wrapper in the mobile SDK to coerce optional complex types into canonical JSON before serialization. for (2) we can extend the error envelope to include tool_return_code and correlation_id — that's a small change but requires a back-compat check.

[05:06] Tom: about telemetry — can Redwood emit sampling hooks or do we need to ship full traces? our budget doesn't allow full sampling.
[05:14] Marcus: runtime supports tail-sampling and probabilistic trace headers. we'll propose a sampling policy you can set per-route.

[05:24] Jordan: cool. recap: Priya -> repro for serialization, Marcus -> runtime flags + sampling policy, Jordan -> pricing sheet + docs, Evan -> run load test and attach traces, Rana -> schedule security deep dive. we'll reconvene next week same time.

[05:40] Rana: one last thing — any known gotchas with KV cache invalidation and canary rollouts? we had an incident where canary users hit stale cache entries after model switch.
[05:48] Priya: yeah model variant pinning + cache namespaces is the recommended pattern — you namespace KV cache by model-version so caches don't collide across rollouts. also put a short TTL for canaries.
[05:58] Evan: great, thanks all.
[06:00] Jordan: thanks everyone, I'll post notes and the links. talk next week.

[06:05] END
